items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Wow. The little Mozart. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, he was great.

ctx.x: because I was the last surviving Napoleon on his side. And he would tell me stories about my father. And he said, “you know when your father was about 18 years old, 19, 18, he bought a trumpet because he wanted to play the trumpet. And he started a jazz club like I forget the name of it now, he told me what the name is I can’t remember, the Arrowsmith or the Arrow Club. And they used to chip in dues to belong to this jazz club, it was a club, you know, a society? And he said he used to put the trumpet in a closet…
